must_not_say: Do not claim Tally can replay historical submissions into a newly listening scenario or make “Run once” process existing responses.
Do not promise that Tally fixes multiple-choice ID-to-text mapping or field-specific Airtable write failures.
Do not claim a downstream automation can return a conditional redirect after submission; only form-side conditional logic and redirect behavior are documented.
Do not claim Tally provides a built-in validation gate for blank fields or a human-review branch.
Do not generalize this proposition beyond no-code automation agencies.
Do not conflate a native connector, a generic automation module, and a custom HTTP webhook endpoint.
Do not omit the webhook endpoint’s 10-second processing-and-response limit.
Do not add pricing, security, AI, file uploads, the wider integration catalog, or customer logos; they distract from the operational test.
Do not manufacture urgency, a recent failure, or an installed Make, Zapier, or n8n stack for the recipient.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
No verified link connects this argument to the proposed buyer problem. Explain only the documented function; do not invent a pain, a switching story or a promised outcome.

Tally documents form-side conditional logic and redirect-on-completion, but the ledger does not show that a downstream automation can return a conditional redirect after webhook submission; webhook processing is also subject to a 10-second.

Webhooks push data when a new submission occurs, and failed attempts can be inspected and retried, but the ledger does not document replaying previously received submissions into a newly listening scenario.
